rows.title: Extension feels slow
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you share the approximate size of the file where typing lags, the steps that trigger it consistently, and your Note Stats and VS Code versions, OS, and whether this is desktop or vscode.dev? Please also check whether the lag remains after running `Extensions: Disable All Installed Extensions` and then enabling only Note Stats. Status bar item does not hide when the last editor is closed
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report. I traced this against current `main`: `onDidChangeActiveTextEditor` calls `refresh()`, which hides the item and returns when `activeTextEditor` is undefined. The document-change listener also cannot show it again in that state because it refreshes only when the changed document is still the active editor. I therefore couldn't reproduce the stale-item path from the current source. If this happens again, a short recording plus the Note Stats version, VS Code version, OS, and whether this is desktop or vscode.dev would help identify an environment-specific event sequence.

rows.title: Word count counts numbers as words
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is the intended counting model: Note Stats treats each whitespace-separated token as a word, including numbers, dates, and standalone punctuation, matching the behavior documented in README.md. That means `3 apples and 2 pears` is five words, while `2026-09-12` or a lone `—` each counts as one. Closing this as designed.

rows.title: Add spell checking to Note Stats
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the suggestion. Spell checking and correction are explicitly outside Note Stats' scope: the project is limited to measuring text and inserting small snippets on request, while https://github.com/egamma/sweeper-sandbox/blob/main/vision.md lists spell checking under "Out of scope." Closing this request so the extension stays within that documented boundary.

rows.title: Is there a keyboard shortcut for Insert Timestamp?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the question. Note Stats does not provide a default shortcut for **Note Stats: Insert Timestamp**. To add your own, open **Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts**, search for `Note Stats: Insert Timestamp`, select the pencil icon, press your preferred key combination, and confirm it. The command ID is `noteStats.insertTimestamp` if you prefer editing `keybindings.json` directly.

rows.title: Doesn't work
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you clarify what does not appear: the Note Stats item in the status bar, the `Note Stats: ...` commands in the Command Palette, or both? Please include the steps you took, whether a text editor was open, what you expected versus what happened, and your Note Stats and VS Code versions and whether this is desktop or vscode.dev. If possible, also check whether it persists with other extensions disabled and Note Stats enabled on its own.

rows.title: Changing noteStats.showCharacters has no effect until the window is reloaded
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the clear report and diagnosis. This reproduces directly from the current source: `noteStats.showCharacters` is read once during activation, and the status-bar refresh keeps using that original value. The setting is intended to apply immediately, so this should remain open as a settings bug until the configuration wiring is updated.

rows.title: Character count setting not applied
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is the same defect as the older, more detailed report at https://github.com/egamma/sweeper-sandbox/issues/4: `noteStats.showCharacters` is read only when the extension activates, so changing it does not update the status bar until the window or extension host reloads. Closing this issue in favor of that canonical report; the restart observation here confirms the same behavior.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report the showCharacters setting having no effect on the status bar until VS Code is reloaded, the same stale read-once-at-activation configuration defect.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This is already tracked by the older, more detailed https://github.com/egamma/sweeper-sandbox/issues/8, which covers showing an estimated reading time alongside the word count and discusses its placement and formatting. Closing this one in favor of that issue; the preference for a concise Medium-like presentation is useful context to retain there.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request the same capability: displaying an estimated reading time derived from word count, which #8 specifies in detail (status bar `~3 min read`) and #9 asks for generically.

rows.title: Word count is wrong when words are separated by more than one space
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the clear report. This is confirmed on current `main`: `computeStats` splits on a literal single space, so `one  two` creates an empty token, while newlines are not handled as word separators. The README specifies whitespace-separated counting matching `wc -w`, so this should stay open as a correctness bug with regression coverage for repeated spaces and blank-line-separated paragraphs.
